abstract: Aging impairs organ regeneration, with insufficient angiogenesis as a key contributor. Here, we show that the endothelial immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 is upregulated in aged mouse livers after partial hepatectomy. Endothelial PSMB8 deletion or PR-957 inhibition promotes angiogenesis and rescues liver regeneration. diGly proteomics identifies TAZ (transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif) as a ubiquitin-dependent immunoproteasome substrate, and TAZ activation restores aged liver regeneration. Aging triggers the infiltration of CD38+IGLC1+ IgM B cells and aberrant perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition in the liver. Recombinant light chain-derived amyloid fibrils directly induce PSMB8 expression in vitro. Anselamimab-mediated light chain-derived amyloid clearance mitigates immunoproteasome overactivation and restores regeneration. Single-cell RNA sequencing confirms that anselamimab reverses aging-induced endothelial marker loss and inflammatory gene upregulation. Our findings establish a pathway linking perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition to regenerative decline via endothelial immunoproteasome activation, suggesting amyloid clearance as a promising therapeutic strategy for aging-associated decline in liver regeneration.
